name: Axis, Symbolic Terrain and Reachability Topology
purpose: Give the project's Axis vocabulary a structured spatial grammar so that North, South, mountain, plane, mud, swamp, roots, Door, leash and cage describe relations, states, flows and constraints rather than becoming loose labels.

mud.role: low-visibility, high-friction substrate from which forms emerge

swamp.role: entangled, stagnant or difficult-to-navigate relational field
swamp.warning: Swamp is a project metaphor. It must not be used to label real people or groups as inherently corrupt.

roots.role: memory, origin, dependency, hidden support and accumulated path history

drain.role: path through which energy, attention, resources or meaning leave a system

leash.role: anchored constraint restricting admissible motion or future states in project geometry
leash.warning: Leash is a project constraint metaphor unless an actual physical tether/constraint is being modeled.

cage.role: feasible region produced by several simultaneous boundaries or constraints
cage.warning: Cage can be symbolic/systemic; do not infer literal imprisonment from topology language.

trajectory_topology.timeline: one admissible path through the state/transition space
trajectory_topology.path_space: set of admissible timelines under declared constraints/dynamics
trajectory_topology.winding: closed paths can carry encirclement/history information around excluded centers
trajectory_topology.homotopy: paths may belong to different deformation classes when obstacles/holes exist
trajectory_topology.reachable_set: states accessible from a starting state under declared controls and constraints
trajectory_topology.target_set: desired/theological/narrative destination must be distinguished from guaranteed outcome
trajectory_topology.dominator: a node/door is mandatory only if every admissible path from source to target passes through it
trajectory_topology.constraint_intersection: multiple leash/boundary regions may intersect into a smaller feasible cage
trajectory_topology.spiral_to_orbit: a widening spiral under a fixed radial leash becomes boundary/tangential motion once the maximum radius is active unless the constraint changes

fate_destiny_topology.possible: target is reachable by at least one admissible path
fate_destiny_topology.inevitable: all admissible paths reach the target in the declared model
fate_destiny_topology.attractor: many trajectories tend toward a set but need not be logically forced
fate_destiny_topology.absorbing: model gives no exit once state is entered
fate_destiny_topology.constrained: some futures are removed while several remain
fate_destiny_topology.theological: providence/predestination/telos remain theological and are not inferred from geometry

spatial_questions: Where is a node relative to the axis?
What terrain does the relationship cross?
What is above, below, inside, outside or at the boundary?
Where are the bottlenecks, bridges, passes and dominators?
What becomes visible only after elevation or separation changes?
What is buried in roots or mud?
What is trapped in a swamp-like feedback loop?
What constraints reduce the reachable set?
Which constraints are slack and which are active?
Does a widening spiral hit a boundary and become an orbit?
Is a claimed destination merely reachable, strongly attracting, probable, or unavoidable on every admissible path?
What Door or release changes the topology or enlarges the viable/reachable region?

implementation.visualization: Use terrain as a semantic layer over the graph; display leash/cage/reachable-region only when the underlying constraint fields are explicitly populated. Do not imply that symbolic terrain is geographic fact.
